extracted.intended_audience: upper-level undergraduate / beginning graduate students studying algebraic topology (covering spaces and fundamental group)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and constructions for existence, uniqueness, and classification of covering spaces of a topological space X (homotopy/path lifting, universal cover construction, correspondence with subgroups of π1, deck transformation groups, and reconstruction from group actions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Homotopy lifting property (covering homotopy property)
rubrics_metrics.description:
Given a covering space p: 
X̃→X, a map f0:Y→X̃ lifting f0 and a homotopy ft:Y→X with f0 = p∘f0, there exists a unique homotopy f̃t:Y→X̃ lifting ft and starting at f̃0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 1.30: this was proved as property (c) in the proof of Theorem 1.7. The homotopy lifting property is the general lifting statement from which path lifting and homotopy-of-paths lifting follow; uniqueness of lifted homotopies follows from uniqueness of lifts on each time-slice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Path lifting property
rubrics_metrics.description: For a covering p: X̃→X and a path f:I→X with f(0)=x0 and a chosen lift x̃0 ∈ p^{-1}(x0), there is a unique path f̃:I→X̃ starting at x̃0 with p∘f̃ = f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the special case of the homotopy lifting property taking Y a point or I. Uniqueness implies every lift of a constant path is constant (or deduce from discreteness of the fiber). Taking Y=I also shows endpoint-preserving homotopies of paths lift to homotopies of lifted paths fixing endpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Injectivity of p_* on π1 and characterization of its image
rubrics_metrics.description: For a covering p:(X̃,x̃0)→(X,x0) the induced map p_*:π1(X̃,x̃0)→π1(X,x0) is injective; its image consists exactly of homotopy classes of loops in X based at x0 whose lifts to X̃ starting at x̃0 are loops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 1.31: kernel elements lift to nullhomotopic loops by homotopy lifting, so p_* injective. Conversely, any loop in the image lifts to a loop; homotopy-lifting shows equivalence. Use this to identify subgroups corresponding to covering spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of sheets equals index of p_*
rubrics_metrics.description: If p:X̃→X is a covering with X path-connected, the number of sheets (cardinality of the fiber p^{-1}(x0)) equals the index [π1(X,x0) : p_*(π1(X̃,x̃0))].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 1.32: define map Φ sending cosets H[g] to endpoints of lifts of g and show it is a bijection onto p^{-1}(x0) using path-connectedness and uniqueness of lifting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lifting criterion for maps (existence of lift)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given covering p:(X̃,x̃0)→(X,x0) and a map f:(Y,y0)→(X,x0) with Y path-connected and locally path-connected, a lift f̃:(Y,y0)→(X̃,x̃0) exists if and only if f_*(π1(Y,y0)) ⊂ p_*(π1(X̃,x̃0)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 1.33: the 'only if' direction is immediate. For the converse construct lifts pointwise via lifting of paths from y0 and show well-definedness using the subgroup condition and homotopy lifting. Continuity uses evenly covered neighborhoods and local path-connectedness of Y. Note: without local path-connectedness this criterion can fail (see exercise reference).

rubrics_metrics.name: Local path-connectedness (definition and role)
rubrics_metrics.description: A space is locally path-connected if each point has arbitrarily small open neighborhoods that are path-connected; this property is required for the lifting criterion and for the classification/construction arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text explains that for Y to be locally path-connected means for each y and neighborhood U there is V⊂U open path-connected. Local path-connectedness ensures path-components are open so basis constructions (e.g., sets U[γ]) form a topology and continuity of lifts can be checked on path-connected neighborhoods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique lifting property for maps (uniqueness of lifts)
rubrics_metrics.description: If p:X̃→X is a covering and f:Y→X with Y connected, then two lifts f̃1,f̃2:Y→X̃ that agree at one point of Y must agree on all of Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 1.34: use evenly covered neighborhoods to show the set where lifts agree is open and closed; connectedness of Y forces equality. This is used repeatedly to show lifts determined by basepoint choice and to argue injectivity of deck actions on fibers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semilocally simply-connected (necessary condition for universal cover)
rubrics_metrics.description: X is semilocally simply-connected if each point x ∈ X has a neighborhood U such that the inclusion-induced map π1(U,x)→π1(X,x) is trivial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This condition is necessary for existence of a simply-connected covering space: loops in U lift to loops in the cover and are nullhomotopic there, so inclusion must be trivial. Locally simply-connected ⇒ semilocally simply-connected; examples and counterexamples (shrinking wedge vs. cone) illustrate the distinction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of universal cover via homotopy classes of paths
rubrics_metrics.description: When X is path-connected, locally path-connected, and semilocally simply-connected, construct X̃ whose points are homotopy classes [γ] of paths γ in X starting at x0, with projection p([γ])=γ(1), and topology generated by sets U[γ] for U in a basis of path-connected opens with trivial π1→π1(X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines U[γ] = {[γ η] | η a path in U starting at γ(1)} and shows these sets form a basis, that p: X̃→X is a covering, and that X̃ is simply-connected (hence the universal cover). The condition (∗) U[γ]=U[γ′] when [γ′]∈U[γ] and the partition property of these sets are crucial.

rubrics_metrics.name: U[γ] basis property and p|_{U[γ]} homeomorphism
rubrics_metrics.description: For U with trivial π1→π1(X), the sets U[γ] partition p^{-1}(U), p maps U[γ] bijectively onto U, and p|_{U[γ]} is a homeomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to show p is a covering map. The equality property U[γ]=U[γ′] if [γ′]∈U[γ] and the way intersections of such basis sets behave are recorded as (∗) and used to verify the topology is well-defined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal cover is simply-connected
rubrics_metrics.description: The constructed space X̃ (points = homotopy classes of paths from x0) is path-connected and π1(X̃,[x0]) is trivial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument: any point [γ] is joined to [x0] by the path t↦[γ_t] where γ_t equals γ on [0,t] and constant afterwards. Injectivity of p_* shows image trivial; lifted loops must be trivial so π1(X̃) = 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of covering space for each subgroup H⊂π1(X) (realizability)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is path-connected, locally path-connected, semilocally simply-connected then for every subgroup H⊂π1(X,x0) there exists a covering space p:X_H→X with p_*(π1(X_H,x̃0)) = H (for suitable basepoint).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 1.36: form quotient of the universal cover by equivalence [γ]~[γ′] iff γ(1)=γ′(1) and [γ γ′]∈H. Show neighborhoods descend and projection X_H→X is a covering with subgroup H.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness (isomorphism) criterion via induced subgroups
rubrics_metrics.description: Two path-connected covering spaces p1:(X1,x1)→(X,x0) and p2:(X2,x2)→(X,x0) are isomorphic (via basepoint-preserving homeomorphism f with p1 = p2∘f) iff p1_*(π1(X1,x1)) = p2_*(π1(X2,x2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 1.37: lifting criterion gives lifts of p1 to X2 and vice versa; unique lifting and basepoint considerations show the lifts are inverses when subgroups agree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification theorem (correspondence with subgroups/conjugacy)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is path-connected, locally path-connected, semilocally simply-connected, basepoint-preserving isomorphism classes of path-connected covering spaces p:(X̃,x̃0)→(X,x0) are in bijection with subgroups of π1(X,x0); ignoring basepoints gives bijection with conjugacy classes of subgroups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 1.38: assembling existence and uniqueness results; changing basepoint in the fiber conjugates the subgroup via the class of a path between basepoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action of π1(X,x0) on the fiber via lifting loops (representation by permutations)
rubrics_metrics.description: For covering p:X̃→X and basepoint x0, each loop γ at x0 induces a permutation L_γ of the fiber p^{-1}(x0) (send a lift's start to its end); γ↦L_γ gives a homomorphism π1(X,x0)→Perm(p^{-1}(x0)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This encoding recovers finite-sheeted covers: n-sheeted covering spaces correspond to homomorphisms π1→Σ_n up to conjugacy. L_{γ·η} = L_γ L_η (with a chosen convention). Examples on S^1 and S^1∨S^1 illustrate the permutations arising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconstruction of covering from an action ρ:π1→Perm(F) (X_ρ construction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an action ρ of π1(X,x0) on discrete set F, form X_ρ as quotient of universal cover × F by identification ([γ],a) ~ ([λγ], ρ(λ)a) for λ∈π1; projection to X is a covering with fiber F and action ρ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows that every action arises from some covering and conversely the covering associated to ρ is isomorphic to the original covering when ρ is the monodromy action. Topology/local homeomorphism properties follow from evenly covered neighborhoods of the universal cover.

rubrics_metrics.name: n-sheeted coverings correspond to homomorphisms π1→Σ_n up to conjugacy
rubrics_metrics.description: n-sheeted covering spaces of X are classified by equivalence classes of homomorphisms ρ:π1(X,x0)→Σ_n where equivalence identifies ρ with conjugates h^{-1}ρh for h∈Σ_n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reduces the geometric classification to a classical algebraic problem about permutation representations of π1. Infinite n permitted (Σ_n as symmetric group on the fiber set).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deck transformations and determination by a point
rubrics_metrics.description: Deck transformations (covering automorphisms) of a covering p:X̃→X are homeomorphisms X̃→X̃ commuting with p; for path-connected covers a deck transformation is determined by the image of any single point, and only the identity can fix a point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group of deck transformations G(X̃) under composition; examples: R→S^1 helix cover gives G≅Z (vertical translations), z↦z^n cover of S^1 gives G≅Z_n (rotations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Normal (regular) covering spaces and equivalence with normal subgroups
rubrics_metrics.description: A covering p:X̃→X is normal (regular) iff for each x∈X and any two lifts x̃,x̃' of x there is a deck transformation taking x̃ to x̃'; equivalently the subgroup H = p_*(π1(X̃,x̃0)) is normal in π1(X,x0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 1.39(a): normal coverings are characterized by H normal. Part (b): deck group G(X̃) ≅ N(H)/H where N(H) is normalizer; for universal cover H trivial so G≅π1(X). Normal covers are those with maximal symmetry; examples and table references given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition (*) for group actions to produce coverings (covering space action)
rubrics_metrics.description: An action of G on Y satisfies (*) if each y∈Y has a neighborhood U such that the images g(U) (g∈G) are pairwise disjoint (g1(U)∩g2(U)≠∅ ⇒ g1=g2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the working definition of a 'covering space action' in the text (not standard everywhere). (*) implies freeness (no nontrivial fixed points) but is stronger than proper discontinuity. Examples: actions with fixed points (tiling symmetries) fail (*); irrational rotation action on S^1 is free but fails (*).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotient by an action satisfying (*) is a normal covering (Proposition 1.40)
rubrics_metrics.description: If G acts on Y satisfying (*), then the quotient map p:Y→Y/G is a normal covering; if Y is path-connected then G is the group of deck transformations of p; and if Y is path-connected and locally path-connected then G ≅ π1(Y/G)/p_*(π1(Y)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: choose U as in (*); quotient identifies disjoint g(U)'s to a single neighborhood, giving evenly covered sets. Each g∈G gives a deck transformation; if Y path-connected all deck transformations arise this way. The last is a restatement of Proposition 1.39 in the action language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper discontinuity and freeness distinctions (anti-patterns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proper discontinuity (each point has neighborhood U with U∩g(U) nonempty for only finitely many g) is weaker than (*); freeness (no nontrivial element fixes any point) does not imply (*).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: symmetry group of hexagonal tiling is properly discontinuous but fails (*) due to fixed points at vertices; irrational rotation action on S^1 is free but orbits are dense so (*) fails. Exercise: on Hausdorff spaces, freeness + proper discontinuity ⇒ (*).
